paragraphs: Ireland needs many workers from outside Europe. A new report from the ESRI says this. The ESRI is a research group.

Every year, Ireland gives 30,000 to 40,000 work permits to these workers. A work permit lets a person work in the country. In 2025, about one in three permits went to people from India. More than 8,000 companies hired workers from outside Europe.
Many of these workers have jobs in hospitals, care homes, building and food. There are not enough workers for these jobs.

But many workers do not stay. Some cannot bring their families. Others find it hard to use their diplomas here. The report says Ireland should make this easier. It also says these workers need better pay and jobs.

經濟與社會研究所（ESRI）的一份新報告這樣說。
ESRI是一個研究機構。
愛爾蘭每年發給這些勞工三萬到四萬張工作許可。
工作許可讓一個人可以在這個國家工作。
2025年，大約三分之一的許可發給了來自印度的人。
超過八千家公司僱用了歐洲以外的勞工。
這些勞工很多在醫院、照護機構、建築業和食品業工作。
這些工作的人手不夠。
但是很多勞工沒有留下來。
有些人不能把家人帶來。
還有些人發現很難在這裡使用他們的文憑。
報告說愛爾蘭應該讓這些事變得更容易。
報告也說這些勞工需要更好的薪水和工作。

paragraphs: Ireland still needs large numbers of workers from outside the European Economic Area (EEA), a new report from the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI) says. But the country has trouble keeping many of them.

Between 30,000 and 40,000 work permits were given or renewed each year for the last four years. In 2025, Indian workers got 32% of permits. Workers from the Philippines and Brazil each got 11%. More than 8,300 companies hired people this way, and Google hired the most.

The number of these workers grew in almost every type of business. Hotels, restaurants and building firms hired many more. There are still not enough workers in health, social care, building, farming and transport.

Many people leave after a short time. Two years after arriving, 40% of workers with a Critical Skills Permit, for jobs that need special skills, have left. Some find it hard to get their qualifications accepted, for example as doctors, nurses or teachers.
The report says Ireland should make it easier for families to join workers, process visas faster, and offer better pay and conditions.

但這個國家很難留住其中許多人。

這類勞工的人數幾乎在每一種行業都增加了。
飯店、餐廳和建築公司僱用了更多人。

持有「關鍵技能許可」（用於需要特殊技能的工作）的勞工中，有40%在抵達兩年後已經離開。
有些人很難讓自己的資格被承認，例如醫生、護理師或教師。
報告說，愛爾蘭應該讓家人更容易來與勞工團聚、加快簽證處理，並提供更好的薪資和條件。

paragraphs: Ireland continues to rely on large numbers of workers from outside the European Economic Area, but struggles to hold on to many of them, according to a new report from the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI).

Between 30,000 and 40,000 employment permits have been issued or renewed in each of the last four years. Indian nationals accounted for 32% of permits in 2025, followed by Filipino and Brazilian workers at 11% each. More than 8,300 firms recruited from outside the EEA last year, with Google at the top of the list.
Recruitment increased in 24 of 25 sectors between 2021 and 2025, with information technology the only exception. Shortages remain in health, social care, construction, agri-food and transport.

Retention is a major concern. Two years after arriving, 40% of Critical Skills Permit holders had left, compared with 21% of those on General Employment Permits. Workers also face difficulties getting foreign qualifications recognised in regulated professions such as medicine, nursing and teaching.
The authors recommend better access to family reunification, faster visa processing, cheaper and quicker recognition of qualifications, and improvements in pay and job quality.

paragraphs: Ireland remains heavily dependent on workers from beyond the European Economic Area, yet is failing to retain a sizeable share of them, a new study by the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI) has found.

Between 30,000 and 40,000 employment permits have been granted or renewed annually over the past four years. Indian nationals accounted for almost a third of permits in 2025, with Filipino and Brazilian workers trailing at 11% apiece. Upwards of 8,300 firms recruited from outside the bloc last year, spearheaded by Google.

Non-EEA hiring surged in all but one of 25 sectors between 2021 and 2025, the sole exception being information technology. Acute shortages persist in healthcare, social care, construction, agri-food and transport.

Retention, however, is a glaring weakness. Within two years, 40% of Critical Skills Permit holders had moved on, roughly double the attrition rate among General Employment Permit holders. Many newcomers also find their credentials stymied by cumbersome recognition procedures in regulated professions such as medicine, nursing and teaching.
The authors urge the State to smooth the path to family reunification, expedite visa processing, streamline recognition of qualifications and bolster pay and working conditions.
